source_file: Berlin 2026 edition for next app devCon 2026 (flutterCon Berlin), sources listed on the page
question: Q5: The Europe Factor

sections.prompt: Raise your hand if you have seen a salary range in a Flutter job ad this year.
sections.hint: EU Pay Transparency Directive: national laws were due 7 June 2026; Germany had no draft in July (Bundestag). Ask whether a range changed a decision.
no_hands: Where do you get salary information today: friends, surveys, recruiters, guesswork?
Would a visible range change which ads you apply to?
For hirers: what holds you back from putting a range in every ad?
hands_up: Did the range change your decision to apply, or your ask in the interview?
Was the range for Flutter different from the native roles you saw?
Was the range honest, or a wide band that said nothing?
follow_ups: Does transparency help juniors or seniors more?
Where should a junior look for a realistic range before interviewing?

sections.prompt: Raise your hand if you work or hire for a company based in another country.
sections.hint: Indeed job postings index, Sep 2026: US software-dev postings up 19% in a year, Germany down 15% to a record low. Ask what makes a skill portable.
no_hands: What would worry you about a fully remote role abroad?
Do European cities compete with each other for Flutter work, or all of them with the US?
For hirers: what stops you hiring across borders: law, time zones, trust, or tax?
hands_up: How did it happen: remote job, relocation, or freelance contract?
What surprised you most: pay, working culture, or paperwork?
Is Flutter a portable skill across markets, or does each market want something else?
follow_ups: Where in Europe is the Flutter demand you actually see?
What would you tell someone in your city who wants to work for a company abroad?

sections.prompt: Raise your hand if the AI Act, Accessibility Act or GDPR put a ticket in your backlog this year.
sections.hint: Accessibility Act: applies since June 2025. EU AI Act: literacy duty since Feb 2025, hiring-tool rules moved to Dec 2027. Ask which became a real ticket.
no_hands: Which rule do you expect to reach your work first?
Is accessibility on your definition of done, or something for later?
For team leads: who on your team knows what the AI Act asks of your app?
hands_up: How big did that ticket turn out to be?
Did the rule change a design decision or a technology decision?
Was Flutter a help or a hindrance: semantics, screen readers, data handling?
follow_ups: Is regulation a competitive advantage for European developers, or just cost?
What is one accessibility fix every Flutter app in the room could ship this month?

wrap_up: Does being in Europe make Flutter a better or a worse bet than in the US, and why?
Which EU rule will shape your next project more than any framework choice?
